description: Single-panel grouped bar chart summarising SEM-EDS micro-area composition of β-Mn in the hardest samples of three Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels. The x-axis carries three element categories — Mn, Al, Cu — and the y-axis is labelled "Atomic percentage (%)" with a 0-40 scale and tick marks at 10, 20, 30 and 40. A numeric value is printed above every bar. The legend in the upper-right encodes 15Al (red), 17Al (blue) and 19Al (yellow). Mn is by far the dominant element: 36.8 at.% (15Al), 36.2 at.% (17Al) and 36.2 at.% (19Al). Al increases monotonically with alloy Al content: 14.3 at.% (15Al), 16.3 at.% (17Al) and 17.5 at.% (19Al). Cu is the lowest and nearly constant: 2.8 at.% (15Al) and 2.6 at.% for both 17Al and 19Al. No error bars are shown. The panel demonstrates that increasing the nominal Al content of the alloy raises the Al dissolved in β-Mn while Mn and Cu contents stay essentially unchanged among the three alloys, which the text links to solid-solution strengthening of β-Mn.

observations.observation: The figure is a single grouped bar chart with three element categories (Mn, Al, Cu) on the x-axis and 'Atomic percentage (%)' on the y-axis scaled 0-40 with ticks at 10, 20, 30 and 40.
The legend contains three entries: 15Al (red bars), 17Al (blue bars) and 19Al (yellow bars).
Mn contents are 36.8 at.% for 15Al, 36.2 at.% for 17Al and 36.2 at.% for 19Al as printed above the bars.
Al contents are 14.3 at.% for 15Al, 16.3 at.% for 17Al and 17.5 at.% for 19Al as printed above the bars.
Cu contents are 2.8 at.% for 15Al, 2.6 at.% for 17Al and 2.6 at.% for 19Al as printed above the bars.
The Al bar height increases monotonically from 15Al to 17Al to 19Al, whereas the Mn bars decrease only slightly and the Cu bars are essentially unchanged.
No error bars or uncertainty ranges are drawn on any bar; only single numeric labels are printed.
The caption states that the figure shows SEM-EDS results for β-Mn in the hardest samples of the 15Al, 17Al and 19Al alloys.

The citing text states that the chemical compositions of β-Mn in the three samples were measured by SEM-EDS and reports Al contents in β-Mn of 14.3 at.%, 16.3 at.% and 17.5 at.% for the 15Al, 17Al and 19Al hardest samples respectively.
The citing text states that the contents of the other elements in the three alloys were very close to each other.
The citing text attributes the slightly higher intrinsic β-Mn hardness with increasing Al to solid-solution strengthening caused by the higher Al dissolved in β-Mn.

measured_quantities: atomic percentage (at.%) of Mn, Al and Cu in β-Mn measured by SEM-EDS
